history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV town 'Warangal' is approximate - the temple stands in Hanamkonda (Hanumakonda), twin city of Warangal. Built in 1163 CE by the Kakatiya king Rudra Deva, this is the finest example of Kakatiya star-shaped (trikuta) architecture: three shrines to Shiva, Vishnu and Surya on a sandbox foundation, hundreds of intricately carved pillars, and a celebrated monolithic black-basalt Nandi. Protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. DATE FLAG: one devotional source gives a broad 1175-1324 CE range; 1163 CE is the widely accepted date.

name: Thousand Pillar Temple
town_description: Hanamkonda, adjoining Warangal in the Hanumakonda district of Telangana, was a capital of the Kakatiya dynasty and is studded with its monuments - the Thousand Pillar Temple being the best preserved.
tradition: Shaivite (Kakatiya Trikuta temple; Shiva with Vishnu and Surya shrines)

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (approx 150 km)
travel.road: On the Warangal-Hanamkonda highway; easy road access from Warangal city; entry free

visitor_information.best_time: October-February; early morning darshan is serene; crowded on festival days
visitor_information.opening_hours: HOURS CONFLICT: templesnow reports 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM; other travel sources report 5:00 AM - 9:00 PM daily - verify before visiting
